- #35326: same core symptom — new session doesn't inherit the launch cwd when attaching to a running daemon

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #18001: [FEATURE]: Implement /loop command for automated iterative task execution — nearly identical proposal for a native `/loop` slash command with count and condition-based retry variants
- #29059: [FEATURE]: Add Dynamic workflows for repeatable multi-step automation (new Claude Code feature) — broader proposal covering loops, parallelism, and orchestration inspired by Claude Code workflows

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #6152: Very similar request — a session context breakdown dialog (inspired by Claude Code's `/context`), showing per-component token usage. It even includes a PoC implementation and has 22 comments.
- #11434: Requests a tool usage breakdown in the context window — overlaps with the tool-definitions component of this proposal.
- #34298: Requests a cached vs. fresh token breakdown in the context meter — overlaps with the cached tokens visibility aspect.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #40331: Requests a configurable TUI keybind to toggle auto-approve permissions — very similar goal of toggling permission mode at runtime without restarting
- #38289: Requests a persistent indicator + real default for auto-accept permissions per session
- #33788: Bug report about the auto-approve permission toggle not working in settings

If your request is specifically about a `/approve on|off` slash command interface (rather than a keybind or settings toggle), please clarify how it differs from the above.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #16992: [FEATURE]: add /btw command — same /btw slash command request for ephemeral questions that don't pollute session history

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #29272: [FEATURE]: Add /simplify skill for automated code review — same concept of a `/simplify` slash command inspired by Claude Code that dispatches concurrent agents for code review and cleanup (closed).

This issue might be related to an existing closed issue. Please check:
- #20870: "feat: add verify subagent (adversarial verifier)" — a closed proposal for a `verify` subagent with an adversarial mindset (read-only + bash for checks/lint/typecheck). The concept overlaps with this request, though the proposed interface differs (subagent invoked by the main agent vs. a user-facing slash command).

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #38710: [FEATURE]: Port Claude Code Security Plugin — also requests security audit/review functionality ported from Claude Code's security workflow, covering the same use case of scanning for vulnerabilities and credential leaks.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Closing this because it only preserves compatibility with databases created by older preview V2 builds. Those builds were not a stable public persistence boundary, and the additional migration-query machinery is not worth carrying forward.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #13003: Open feature request for displaying token usage in the TUI, including a proposed `/usage` or `/tokens` slash command with per-message breakdown and cost estimation — very similar scope.
- #29634: Closed feature request for a `\usage` command in the CLI showing token usage, estimated cost, and usage by model — nearly identical proposal.
- #10240: Closed feature request for a `/stats` slash command covering token summaries and cost estimates per session.

Please review these issues to see if your request has already been addressed or is being tracked elsewhere.

Complementary: my open PR #41723 covers the other half of the attachment lowering gap — image mimes outside the provider-supported set (`image/avif`, `image/tiff`) currently fall through `attachmentContent` and are silently dropped, while the TUI still labels them `[Image N]`. Thanks for the report. OpenCode's `apply_patch` is based primarily on Codex's tool and intentionally follows the same relevant execution semantics: file operations are applied sequentially, and a later filesystem failure may leave an earlier committed prefix in place.

Models are trained and post-trained around these tool semantics. Atomic multi-file filesystem transactions and rollback would be a new contract rather than a correctness fix, and we don't plan to diverge from Codex here right now.

Closing as not planned. OpenCode's `apply_patch` is based primarily on Codex's tool and intentionally follows the same relevant execution semantics: operations are sequential and partial application is allowed when a later filesystem mutation fails. Atomic rollback is not part of the tool contract.

The stale-content reproduction described here also does not match the current implementation. OpenCode reads and derives all requested file changes before beginning filesystem mutations, so a stale or invalid later hunk fails verification before the earlier delete is performed. A true later I/O failure can leave earlier operations committed, which is expected behavior.

For anyone hitting the cold-cache npm hang: the same unguarded install exists on v2 — `Npm.reify` runs Arborist with no timeout. I filed #41934 and opened PR #41936 which bounds installs with `Effect.timeout` (default 300s, matching npm's own fetch timeout, configurable via `OPENCODE_NPM_INSTALL_TIMEOUT`) and surfaces timeouts as typed `InstallFailedError` with the package and install directory instead of a silent hang.

Addressed by #41789. V2 canonical message lowering now decodes durable local `file:` source URIs and includes the resolved directory path in reference context while preserving the attachment content and alias. Focused prompt and provider-boundary tests cover the reference-shaped directory case on POSIX and Windows. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #41929. New-session location is now an explicit client-local setting: `launch` is the default and creates `/new` sessions in the TUI invocation directory, while users can opt into `inherit` for the prior behavior. The full TUI and Mini share the same policy, with focused config/runtime tests. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #41793. Managed service contenders now retain a bounded stderr tail and append it to nonzero-exit/signal startup failures, so port conflicts surface the existing actionable remediation instead of only `Server process exited with code 1`. Effect, Promise, and real CLI boundary regressions cover the behavior. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #41788. Ancestor `.claude` and `.agents` skill sources are now registered farthest-to-nearest, so existing later-source precedence selects the worktree-local duplicate instead of the parent checkout copy. The exact nested-worktree regression failed before the change and passes afterward. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #41782. ACP session creation now persists a model variant only when the catalog explicitly declares a `default`; it no longer chooses the first displayed effort such as `none`. The ACP control still lists available efforts without sending an unsolicited variant, covered by focused lifecycle and config-option tests. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #41780. Bedrock Converse lowering now merges adjacent canonical user/tool-result content into the single user message required after parallel tool use. The exact two-tool regression was reproduced as HTTP 400 before the fix and recorded as HTTP 200 with a successful continuation afterward. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.
